question: How should the best practitioner offer food, and what substitute is used if no vessel is available?
premises: The best practitioner should scatter the food offerings in front until satisfaction is complete.
If no vessel is available, a substitute must be used.
The substitute is the bhadra or the rolled shell.
inference: Food offerings are scattered until satiation, and in the absence of a vessel the hand-gestures bhadra or rolled shell serve as substitutes.
uncertainties: Whether bhadra and vellitā-śukti are alternatives or used together is clarified in the next verses.
plain_english: There the best practitioner should scatter the offerings in front until complete satisfaction; if no vessel is available, he should use the bhadra or the rolled shell.
